name_devanagari: चिपुर् जगन्नात महाडेव विष्णु मन्डिर || DDL0291
description_en: A Viṣṇuśikharatemple from approx. 14th-15th.The temple is within the Jagannātha temple complex, 1,5 kilometres south-east from Chipur.The temple is built in thelatina nāgaramode. It is constituted of anardhamaṇḍapa(pillared portico). The portico is surmounted by a large pediment (śukanāsikā). The door of the temple is oriented to the east-south-east. On the north-western wall is a small altar with sculptures of different time periods. Each outer wall has a carved niche. Theśikharais topped by anāmalakaring, surmounted by a metal finial.The stone sculptures inside the temple may come from different monuments. At the base of the sanctum's altar is a small niche containing a stone image that appears to represent Sūrya (005). D. R. Sharma identifies the monument as a Vaishnava temple (Sharma 2012, p. 290-291). This affiliation is probably dur to the magnificient, although damaged movable image of Viṣṇu (001). The temple is built on the same layout as theśikharain Devala Hāṭa (BTD0030) and may be approximately dated from the 14th-15th century.
references: REFERENCES Sharma, Dilli Raj. 2012. Heritage of Western Nepal. Art and Architecture . Kathmandu: Centre for Nepal and Asian Studies.
